features.title: Create local-first runnable skeleton
features.description: Turn the repository into a recoverable local-first app skeleton for the podcast summarizer rewrite, with root init verifying backend, frontend, harness, and a deterministic smoke path without live OpenAI credentials.
acceptance: Root ./init.sh runs harness verification plus project-owned backend and frontend verification from a fresh checkout.
The project has documented local environment files and scripts for running backend and frontend locally.
A deterministic smoke check proves at least one backend endpoint or core function runs without requiring OPENAI_API_KEY.
The skeleton does not require Postgres, Valkey, Redis, cache services, or remote deployment configuration.

features.title: Remove cloud and non-SQLite runtime paths
features.description: Simplify the existing project to the accepted local-first scope by removing or neutralizing remote deployment, Postgres, Valkey, Redis, cache, and cloud-mode assumptions.
acceptance: Runtime configuration exposes SQLite as the only database target.
Project docs and examples no longer instruct users to deploy remotely or configure Postgres, Valkey, Redis, or cache services.
Docker and local scripts start only the services required for local frontend/backend operation.
Tests or static checks prevent reintroducing required non-SQLite storage in the default runtime.

features.title: Implement SQLite podcast processing model
features.description: Define and implement SQLite persistence for episodes, processing jobs, audio chunks, transcript segments, summary segments, and transcript-to-summary mappings.
acceptance: SQLite schema or migrations create tables for episodes, processing status, chunks, transcript segments, summary segments, and mapping records.
Go repository code can create, read, update, and query the processing entities needed by the pipeline.
Persistence tests cover normal writes, status transitions, lookup by podcast URL, and transcript-summary mapping retrieval.
Local data paths are documented and ignored from git where appropriate.

features.title: Add podcast URL ingestion and idempotency
features.description: Implement backend ingestion for a submitted podcast URL, including duplicate detection so existing episodes are returned without re-running the processing pipeline.
acceptance: Submitting a new podcast URL creates an episode or processing job record.
Submitting an already known URL returns the existing episode state without downloading, chunking, transcribing, or summarizing again.
The ingestion logic records clear statuses and errors for new and duplicate submissions.
Backend tests prove duplicate submissions are idempotent.

features.title: Download and chunk podcast audio locally
features.description: Implement local audio download and chunking for accepted podcast URLs, storing artifacts under project-owned local data directories.
acceptance: The backend downloads episode audio into a documented local data directory.
Audio chunk metadata is persisted with stable ordering and local file references.
Chunking can run through a documented local tool or internal implementation with clear setup guidance.
Tests or fixtures verify chunk ordering, persisted metadata, and failure handling without requiring a large real podcast file.

features.title: Add OpenAI transcription adapter
features.description: Implement the real transcription adapter using OpenAI while preserving fixture-backed tests that do not require live network calls.
acceptance: The backend exposes a transcription interface with an OpenAI implementation selected by configuration.
OpenAI credentials and model configuration are documented in .env.example and README guidance.
Transcription results are stored as ordered transcript segments with timing or chunk association metadata.
Adapter tests use fixtures or test doubles and do not require a live OPENAI_API_KEY.

features.title: Add OpenAI summarization and transcript mapping
features.description: Implement OpenAI-backed summarization that groups one or more transcript paragraphs into summary segments and persists the mapping between summaries and source transcript segments.
acceptance: The backend exposes a summarization interface with an OpenAI implementation selected by configuration.
Summary generation accepts transcript segments and produces ordered summary segments.
Each summary segment records which transcript segment IDs or paragraph groups it summarizes.
Tests verify grouping and mapping behavior with deterministic fixtures and no live OpenAI call.

features.title: Orchestrate podcast processing pipeline
features.description: Connect ingestion, download, chunking, transcription, summarization, persistence, and failure handling into a resumable local processing pipeline.
acceptance: A submitted new episode can progress through download, chunking, transcription, summarization, and completion statuses.
Failures are persisted with enough information for the admin UI and logs to explain the failed stage.
Pipeline retries or restarts do not duplicate completed artifacts for an already processed episode.
A deterministic end-to-end backend test exercises the pipeline using local fixtures.

features.title: Expose local backend API
features.description: Provide HTTP APIs for admin submission, processing status, episode listing, and episode transcript-summary retrieval.
acceptance: The backend has an endpoint to submit a podcast URL and return the existing or newly created episode/job.
The backend has endpoints for episode status, episode list, and detailed transcript-summary data.
API responses include enough structured data for the frontend to render admin status and episode viewer mapping.
HTTP handler tests cover success, duplicate submission, not found, and failed processing responses.

features.title: Build admin podcast submission UI
features.description: Build a frontend admin page for submitting podcast URLs, seeing whether an episode already exists, and inspecting processing status or errors.
acceptance: The admin page provides a podcast URL input and submit action wired to the backend API.
Submitting an existing episode shows the existing episode state instead of implying a new processing run started.
The page displays processing stage, completion, and failure states clearly.
Frontend tests or interaction checks cover submit, duplicate, loading, success, and error states.

features.title: Build transcript and summary viewer
features.description: Build the episode viewer that presents transcript paragraphs or paragraph groups together with their corresponding summary segments.
acceptance: The viewer fetches episode detail data from the backend API.
Transcript segments are displayed in reading order with associated summary content visible near or alongside the relevant paragraphs.
The UI handles loading, empty, failed, and completed episode states.
Frontend tests or interaction checks prove transcript-summary mapping is rendered from fixture API data.

features.title: Polish local Docker demo and documentation
features.description: Finalize local Docker workflow, README guidance, demo fixtures, and portfolio-focused documentation for the rewritten podcast summarizer.
acceptance: Docker or Docker Compose starts the local backend and frontend without remote deployment services.
README explains local setup, OpenAI configuration, deterministic demo mode, data directories, and the non-production portfolio scope.
Obsolete deployment instructions are removed or clearly marked out of scope.
A final local verification command proves the documented demo path works.
